articles.title: ITR filing deadline: Can freelancers declare earnings as business income? Tax experts explain
articles.summary: Freelance income cannot always be reported as business income in ITR filings. Here is when earnings qualify as business income, salary, or other sources; common filing mistakes; presumptive taxation rules; and expert tips to avoid tax notices and ensure compliance before the 31 July deadline.

articles.title: ITR filing 2026: Why 31 July is not the deadline for all salaried taxpayers and who gets more time
articles.summary: The 31 July ITR filing deadline may not apply to all salaried taxpayers. The applicable due date depends on the taxpayer’s overall income profile, ITR form, and audit requirements. Those with business or professional income may get additional time.

articles.title: Filed ITR in May or June? Here's why you should revisit it and check these 7 key things before 31 July deadline
articles.summary: Taxpayers who filed their ITR in May or June should revisit their return before the 31 July deadline. Checking e-verification status, AIS, TIS, Form 26AS, TDS credits, bank details and reported income can help avoid errors and refund delays.

articles.title: ITR filed and verified? Here's how the Income Tax Department spots mismatches—and when it sends a notice
articles.summary: The CPC first verifies that you've used the correct ITR form, filled in all mandatory schedules, and that there are no calculation errors. If it finds major issues, you may receive a defective return notice.

articles.title: Tax consultant made error in ITR filing: ITAT Chennai gives relief to taxpayer, waives ₹1.92 lakh penalty
articles.summary: A Chennai taxpayer faced a ₹1.92 lakh penalty after her tax consultant made errors in the ITR filing. ITAT Chennai waived the penalty, ruling that a genuine mistake by a tax professional cannot be treated as misreporting of income under Section 270A.

articles.title: Would your family know how to access your wealth in an emergency?

articles.title: SIP reduces only entry-timing risk: Here's why valuation, liquidity and portfolio concentration still need attention
articles.summary: SIPs help reduce entry-timing risk through rupee-cost averaging but cannot shield investors from valuation, liquidity, concentration or fund-selection risks. Investors should not mistake SIPs for a complete risk-management strategy.
